messages.content: I've changed my mind, can I get a greens instead of what I previously ordered?

function.name: ChaFod
function.description: Changes the selection of food based on the customer's request, ensuring the food name provided is in uppercase as per the requirement. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

TheFod.description: The name of the food to be changed, provided in uppercase letters only (e.g., 'PIZZA', 'BURGER').

message.reasoning: We need to respond to user request: "I've changed my mind, can I get a greens instead of what I previously ordered?" They want to change their order to "greens". We have a function ChaFod that changes the selection of food based on the customer's request, ensuring the food name provided is in uppercase as per the requirement. The function accepts a parameter TheFod which can be one of "PIZZA", "BURGER", "SALAD", "SOUP", "STEAK". But the user wants "greens". That is not in the allowed list. The function only accepts those options. So we cannot fulfill "greens" because it's not in the list. We should respond that we cannot process that request because "greens" is not an available option. Or we could ask if they mean "SALAD"? But the user explicitly says "greens". We might interpret "greens" as "SALAD" but we can't guess. We should politely say we cannot process that request because "greens" is not an available option. Alternatively, we could ask them to choose from the available options. The user might want "SALAD" or "SOUP" or "STEAK" etc. But we should not guess. So we respond that we cannot process that request because "greens" is not an available option.
